haiku-low.q1: Only the most recent missed fire time runs, as pending (or skipped if a run is active). Earlier missed fire times are dropped silently, with no row.
haiku-low.q2: A skipped run row is inserted for the new fire time, with finished_at set. It never executes.
haiku-low.q3: Up to 3 attempts. Retry waits 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2. After the third failure the run becomes failed.
haiku-low.q4: After the attempt's heartbeat is over 2 minutes old, the reaper marks it presumed_dead and another worker may retry. That attempt counts toward the 3.
haiku-low.q5: The running job finishes normally. The pending run becomes cancelled. Fire times during the pause get no runs; on resume nothing is caught up.
haiku-low.q6: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on the schedule row means only one worker processes a schedule at a time. The unique (schedule_id, fire_time) constraint is a backstop.
haiku-low.q7: In job_schedules.next_fire_at, in UTC. It moves forward after each tick processes the schedule, and is recomputed on re-enable or tenant resume.
haiku-low.q8: In one transaction, the worker locks one claimable pending run with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, sets it running, increments attempt_count, and inserts an attempt row.
haiku-low.q9: In run_attempts.last_heartbeat_at, updated every 30 seconds. The reaper on each tick finds running attempts whose heartbeat is over 2 minutes old.
haiku-low.q10: In job_runs.next_attempt_at, set to now plus backoff while the run stays pending. It is claimable once next_attempt_at is at or before now().
haiku-low.q11: One job_runs row per fire time, enforced by UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time). One run_attempts row per execution try.
haiku-low.q12: Every worker write requires WHERE id = attempt AND outcome = 'running'. After presumed_dead, a late write matches zero rows, so it cannot overwrite the outcome.

sonnet.q1: Only one run: for the latest missed fire time L (<= now). The earlier missed fire times are dropped silently with no history row. next_fire_at then moves to the first fire time after now().
sonnet.q2: A run row for that fire time is inserted with status 'skipped' and finished_at = now(). It never executes.
sonnet.q3: Up to 3 attempts. Wait is 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2 (counted from when the failure is recorded). After the 3rd failure the run becomes 'failed' with finished_at set.
sonnet.q4: Once its heartbeat is more than 2 minutes old, the reaper (run on each worker's 15-second tick) marks the attempt presumed_dead, so a retry can happen (after the same backoff as a failure; the run goes back to pending). Yes, the dead attempt counts as one of the 3 attempts.
sonnet.q5: The running job is not touched and finishes normally. The pending (waiting to start) job becomes cancelled with finished_at set. No fire times are caught up after resuming: next_fire_at is recomputed as the first fire time after now(), so fire times during the pause are never created.
sonnet.q6: The due-schedule select uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so only one worker holds the schedule row and the other skips it. Backstops: UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and the partial unique index allowing one pending/running run per schedule.
sonnet.q7: In job_schedules.next_fire_at (UTC timestamptz). It is advanced by the tick to the first fire time after now() after a run is created or skipped. It is recomputed (first fire time after now()) when a schedule is enabled or a tenant is resumed. It only moves forward.
sonnet.q8: In one transaction it locks one claimable run with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (status pending, next_attempt_at <= now(), schedule enabled, tenant not paused). It sets status to running, increments attempt_count, inserts a run_attempts row with outcome running, and sets current_attempt_id. Other workers skip the locked row.
sonnet.q9: In run_attempts.last_heartbeat_at, updated by the worker every 30 seconds while outcome = 'running'. The reaper, run by each worker every tick, finds running attempts whose heartbeat is more than 2 minutes old and marks them presumed_dead.
sonnet.q10: In job_runs: status goes back to pending and next_attempt_at = now() + backoff. The run is claimable once next_attempt_at <= now(), and a worker claims it as normal (a new attempt starts).
sonnet.q11: One job_runs row per fire time (UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time)). One run_attempts row per execution try (max 3 per run).
sonnet.q12: Fencing: every worker write is WHERE id = :attempt AND outcome = 'running' (attempt ID is the fencing token). Once the attempt is presumed_dead, the late success matches zero rows, so it cannot overwrite the outcome, and the run row is changed only when the attempt update matched. Races are serialized by the row lock.
